messages:
Zoe (Design): Quick UX flag from testing on small phones: action chips in the compact header are collapsing into two rows and the second row overlaps the first table row during fast scrolls. Screenshot: https://img.redwood/mock/compact-header-overlap.png
Marcus (Product): Does this happen only when there are >3 chips? Which breakpoints?
Zoe (Design): Repro at <= 380px when there are 3+ chips and a visible left rail. The chips wrap and push the sticky header causing a jump.
Ilan (Frontend): Likely the chips use inline-flex + flex-wrap. We can either force nowrap + horizontal scroll, or move less-important chips into an overflow menu.
Priya (Mobile): On Android WebView horizontal scrolling works but momentum can hide the overflow affordance. On iOS Safari it snaps differently.
Marcus (Product): Preference? Keep actions discoverable but avoid layout shifts.
Zoe (Design): My proposal: primary CTA stays full label; secondary actions become icon-only at <=360px; remaining actions go into a "More actions" overflow. Keep hit-targets 44px.
Ilan (Frontend): Implementation plan: detect strip width at render; if overflow, toggle `.compact-mode` which applies icons-only + overflow. Add `aria-label="Action strip"` and make overflow keyboard accessible.
Priya (Mobile): Also add `overscroll-behavior: contain` and `-webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch` if we allow horizontal scrolling. For WebView, ensure we don't rely solely on CSS to compute space (JS feature-detect overflow).
Zoe (Design): Copy nit: label overflow button "More actions" not "More". Tooltip on long-press shows full label.
Ilan (Frontend): Accessibility: overflow trigger should have `aria-haspopup="true"` and update `aria-expanded`. Truncated chip text should expose full content via `aria-label` or `aria-describedby`.
A11y-Bot: Automated check: recommend announcing mode switch with `aria-live="polite"` and ensuring contrast of icon-only chips >= 4.5. Logged RDC-A11Y-333.
Marcus (Product): Next steps: Zoe mock icons-only + overflow, Ilan prototype width-detection + fallback, Priya test on WKWebView and Android. Tagging for next sprint if prototype stable.
Zoe (Design): I'll upload mocks and add microcopy suggestions. Also will include a tiny onboarding dot for the first time the overflow appears.
Ilan (Frontend): I'll push a small branch with the width-detect heuristics and a quick CSS prototype. Will link RDC-1508 when created.
Priya (Mobile): I'll validate gestures on Pixel 4a and iPhone SE and report any quirks.
Marcus (Product): Thanks team ":thumbsup:" — putting this on the roadmap and marking customer-impact low-medium for now.
